<thought>Based on the molecular ion (m/z ≈ 100.05) the formula is C₅H₈O₂ (two degrees of unsaturation, consistent with one C=C and one C=O). The ¹H NMR shows a terminal alkene (CH₂ = CH‑), a CH attached to oxygen (δ ≈ 4.4 ppm) coupled to a methyl group (δ ≈ 2.9 ppm, dd), indicating an O‑CH(CH₃) fragment. This fits the structure of an acrylate ester where the alcohol part is a secondary alcohol (‑O‑CH(CH₃)‑). The SMILES that matches these features and the formula C₅H₈O₂ is **C=CC(=O)OC(C)**.**</thought>
<final_answer>C=CC(=O)OC(C)</final_answer>
